BU 1000 - Introduction to Financial Topics
Credits: 1
This course introduces fundamental financial concepts. It provides students with crucial knowledge and skills to make
informed decisions to promote financial health and prosperity in personal and business settings. The course decodes
and explains complex financial concepts, and helps students develop actionable strategies for managing their
finances,Students will learn how choices influence career options, and future earning potential. Students will also learn
to apply decision-making skills to evaluate career choices and set personal goals. Upon completion of the course,
students should have a working knowledge of the basic financial skills needed to help them achieve financial
independence and success.
When Offered:
Summer Only
BU 1500 - Business in American Society
Credits: 4
The course is designed to introduce the history of U.S. Business and its concepts and functions. It examines external and
internal economic, global, and demographic factors that influence the role of business on a societal and individual level.
Topics include ethical challenges, types of business organizations, entrepreneurship, managerial functions, the creation
of needs and wants via the marketing mix, the interpretation of financial information and wealth creation, and the role
of human resources and labor in contemporary business. Offers an overview of U.S. business and an introduction to the
origins of its specialized areas (e.g., accounting, finance, marketing, operations, management), and their influence in
North American society. Emphasis is placed on the management of these functions in a global, multicultural, team-based
environment and the development of a proactive approach to the dynamic nature of the place of business in

BU 3150 - Topics in Technology Disruptions, AI and Innovation
Credits: 2
Technology disruption and innovation have changed the way workplaces function. Digital technologies have affected
us in that we can no longer use one toolset our whole career and we need to adapt to an ever-changing landscape for
work and life. These technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), mobile applications, marketing systems, and
extensions, to name a few, have changed how we interact with software. We now expect everything to be connected to
online systems that can be changed daily, and if it isn’t web or mobile-supported, we think it’s outdated. This is the tip
of the iceberg technology and innovation are the cornerstones of how knowledge workers are going to function in
business. As we see the landscape changing we need to provide students with knowledgeable skill sets that will give
them technology expertise on a wide variety of these business systems. Understanding these may give us insight on the
new challenges that affect intellectual property, business analytics and data security. The toolsets that are available are
vast and include new GPT clients, interfacing systems for marketing, automation, augmented reality, and mobile device
apps. The ability to provide a foundation-level usage of these technologies will open their skill set to list a variety of
current industry software systems to their resumes. If we look at the Google Suite as a required prerequisite for students
coming out of any university and Excel for an accounting student, these tools are the standard today, but future toolsets
provide students with a well-rounded approach that opens doors. Students need to have a holistic approach to software
and applications that can be utilized in any application that is presented to them. This class is a hands on learning class
where students will specifically work with software such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), mobile apps, web apps, canva,
google suite, and Microsoft 365. To understand the standard and specialized software that is required knowledge in
business. By learning the methods and tools students will be well equipped to apply these tools in their jobs. I used to
run innovation at Stony Brook University, and every business student who worked for me learned 3D printing. Even if it
was something, they didn’t have to learn from their major. Numerous of them have told me how they were asked about
the use of the technology on their resumes. It was a skill that showed analytical thinking from a technology perspective.
The tools available on the web are vast. We will only be able to touch on the software that is widely used but the
students will be working on projects that will investigate AI use cases such as software that could assist them in turning
any PDF into a PowerPoint file. These a free tools they will navigate that demonstrate the new business model that is
appealing to the next generation. Understanding the business model and technological use will allow them to see how
future revenue models may affect their purchasing decisions as leaders in their careers. We need to give our students
this technology perspective that ensures they have the basics as well as the details to succeed in the new marketplace.

BU 3250 - Business Analytics
Credits: 4
This course prepares students to collect, describe, analyze and forecast data with a primary focus on data analysis,
decision making, and managing uncertainty. Using advanced statistical tools and case study methodology, students will

exposure to a variety of software packages utilized in today’s business environment.

BU 3911 - Business Presentation Skills
Credits: 2
Presentation skills are critical in business to inform and motivate a range of audiences, from clients and investors to

improve their ability to speak with confidence, poise, clarity, and conviction.

Credits: 4

BU 5710 - Financial Modeling and Forecasting
Credits: 4
The course is aimed at giving students a working knowledge of the analytical tools that are important in the decisions
firms regularly make Emphasis will be placed on the performance goals of the firm, the forecasting of investment
returns and firm cash flows, and the estimation of investment firm risk parameters. Regression analysis, along with
other statistical modeling tools where necessary, will be used to estimate relationships among economic variables, and as
a forecasting tool. The course is aimed at consolidating knowledge gained in other functional areas of business. While
knowledge of quantitative techniques is presupposed, the emphasis is more on economic intuition as a practical
problem-solving tool.
Prerequisites

, PE 2430

Credits: 4
Study of theories, techniques and approaches for determining the values of major types of securities including
derivation of capitalization rates, forecasting of earnings and technical analysis. Evaluation of the dividend, capital
leverage controversies and the efficient market hypothesis. Introduction to modern portfolio theories and investment
strategies.

records.title: Introduction to Financial Topics
records.sourceText:
Credits: 1
This course introduces fundamental financial concepts. It provides students with crucial knowledge and skills to make
informed decisions to promote financial health and prosperity in personal and business settings. The course decodes
and explains complex financial concepts, and helps students develop actionable strategies for managing their
finances,Students will learn how choices influence career options, and future earning potential. Students will also learn
to apply decision-making skills to evaluate career choices and set personal goals. Upon completion of the course,
students should have a working knowledge of the basic financial skills needed to help them achieve financial
independence and success.
When Offered:
Summer Only

records.title: Business in American Society
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The course is designed to introduce the history of U.S. Business and its concepts and functions. It examines external and
internal economic, global, and demographic factors that influence the role of business on a societal and individual level.
Topics include ethical challenges, types of business organizations, entrepreneurship, managerial functions, the creation
of needs and wants via the marketing mix, the interpretation of financial information and wealth creation, and the role
of human resources and labor in contemporary business. Offers an overview of U.S. business and an introduction to the
origins of its specialized areas (e.g., accounting, finance, marketing, operations, management), and their influence in
North American society. Emphasis is placed on the management of these functions in a global, multicultural, team-based
environment and the development of a proactive approach to the dynamic nature of the place of business in

contemporary society.
Prerequisites
ECI
When Offered:
Spring Only

records.title: Information Systems for Managers
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Introduction to the concept of information systems as strategic assets of the enterprise utilized to achieve strategic
advantage. Investigation is also made of the use of information systems at the tactical and support business levels.
Technology is always discussed in terms of its interaction with human systems (socio-technical systems). The goals are
to facilitate management decision processes and to exploit information technology for strategic advantage.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Information Technology and Applications
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The purpose of this course is to provide the student with the requisite skills needed to complete technology-based
assignments in accounting and business courses, obtain the necessary skills expected of entry-level accountants and
financial managers (0-2 years) and help prepare students for technology-related subjects tested in professional
certification exams (e.g., CPA, CMA, and CIA).
Prerequisites
MA 2000
Applied Statistics or equivalent

When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Topics in Technology Disruptions, AI and Innovation
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Technology disruption and innovation have changed the way workplaces function. Digital technologies have affected
us in that we can no longer use one toolset our whole career and we need to adapt to an ever-changing landscape for
work and life. These technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), mobile applications, marketing systems, and
extensions, to name a few, have changed how we interact with software. We now expect everything to be connected to
online systems that can be changed daily, and if it isn’t web or mobile-supported, we think it’s outdated. This is the tip
of the iceberg technology and innovation are the cornerstones of how knowledge workers are going to function in
business. As we see the landscape changing we need to provide students with knowledgeable skill sets that will give
them technology expertise on a wide variety of these business systems. Understanding these may give us insight on the
new challenges that affect intellectual property, business analytics and data security. The toolsets that are available are
vast and include new GPT clients, interfacing systems for marketing, automation, augmented reality, and mobile device
apps. The ability to provide a foundation-level usage of these technologies will open their skill set to list a variety of
current industry software systems to their resumes. If we look at the Google Suite as a required prerequisite for students
coming out of any university and Excel for an accounting student, these tools are the standard today, but future toolsets
provide students with a well-rounded approach that opens doors. Students need to have a holistic approach to software
and applications that can be utilized in any application that is presented to them. This class is a hands on learning class
where students will specifically work with software such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), mobile apps, web apps, canva,
google suite, and Microsoft 365. To understand the standard and specialized software that is required knowledge in
business. By learning the methods and tools students will be well equipped to apply these tools in their jobs. I used to
run innovation at Stony Brook University, and every business student who worked for me learned 3D printing. Even if it
was something, they didn’t have to learn from their major. Numerous of them have told me how they were asked about
the use of the technology on their resumes. It was a skill that showed analytical thinking from a technology perspective.
The tools available on the web are vast. We will only be able to touch on the software that is widely used but the
students will be working on projects that will investigate AI use cases such as software that could assist them in turning
any PDF into a PowerPoint file. These a free tools they will navigate that demonstrate the new business model that is
appealing to the next generation. Understanding the business model and technological use will allow them to see how
future revenue models may affect their purchasing decisions as leaders in their careers. We need to give our students
this technology perspective that ensures they have the basics as well as the details to succeed in the new marketplace.

Prerequisites
English Proficiency; Math Proficiency, TBD
When Offered:
Every Semester

records.title: Business Analytics
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course prepares students to collect, describe, analyze and forecast data with a primary focus on data analysis,
decision making, and managing uncertainty. Using advanced statistical tools and case study methodology, students will
be challenged to make economic and financial decisions involving large data sets. Topics include probability, statistics,
data visualization, regression, data mining, and modeling. Additionally, students will develop technological agility from
exposure to a variety of software packages utilized in today’s business environment.
Prerequisites
Minimum grade of “C”in MA 2080
& MA 2000

records.title: Principles of Accounting I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Introduction to financial accounting with focus on how financial statements are structured and used by proprietorships
and corporations. Topics: double entry, accrual accounting, service vs. merchandise companies, cash, accounts receivable
and payable, inventories, fixed assets and depreciation methods, and net earnings. Develops foundation for subsequent
courses in accounting, finance, MIS, and management.
Prerequisites
MA 1020

When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Principles of Accounting II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 3
Emphasis shifts from accounting theory (Principles I) to giving students experience in preparation of financial
statements. New topics include payroll, stockholders’ equity, earnings per share, long-term debt, marketable securities,
and statement of cash flows. The course also includes management topics, including job order costing, process costing,
cost-volume- profit analysis, budgeting, and planning for capital investments.
Prerequisites
BU 3502
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Principles of Business Law
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
A study of the nature and functions of law introducing the student to the legal system, constitutional, administrative,
tort, criminal, consumer protection, employment, and contract law.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Intermediate Business Law
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2

An in-depth study of the law of contracts, agency, and partnerships.
Prerequisites
BU 3600
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Advanced Business Law
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
The study of real and personal property, bailment, documents of title, bankruptcy, secured transactions, and trusts and
estates.
Prerequisites
BU 3605
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Marketing: Principles and Concepts
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
A comprehensive introduction to marketing principles with emphasis on the marketing concept as means of distributing
goods and services in a competitive economy. Examines market determination and population segmentation for product
planning, product distribution systems, pricing policies and practices, and promotion strategies.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Business Communications
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
This course is an introduction to the fundamentals of business communications. It emphasizes planning, research,
organization, clarity, conciseness, positive tone, mechanics and format. Business letters, electronic communications,
memos, and reports will be written and analyzed. Replaces BU 3900.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Business Presentation Skills
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Presentation skills are critical in business to inform and motivate a range of audiences, from clients and investors to
management and staff. Effective speakers, coupled with other essential skills, tend to move up the corporate ladder to
increasing responsibility and success. This course provides the foundations for delivering professional business
presentations. The course will explore verbal and nonverbal skills, delivery techniques, and presentation structure.
Through repeated stand-and -deliver exercises, students will put these techniques into practice, test approaches, and
improve their ability to speak with confidence, poise, clarity, and conviction.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
(offered occasionally)

records.title: Web Systems and Electronic Commerce
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course covers the basics of web systems, furthering an understanding of them through the development of e-
commerce applications and systems. The course provides an overview of several current web technologies, including

client side applications such as web design using JavaScript and VBScript and server side applications on Apache
(Linux) and IIS (Windows) using CGI, ASP , and Java Servlet technologies. Students will implement an e-commerce
application using the learned components involved in a web system and e-business strategies. Projects are carried out
individually and in groups.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every year.

records.title: Organizational Behavior and Management
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course examines the evolution of organizations and managerial roles in contemporary organizations. It provides a
comprehensive analysis of the functions and processes of management. Topics include the influence of business on
society, international business, the managerial functions of planning, organizing, leading, and control, and the social
influence of management in terms of ethics, leadership, power, communication, conflict, and organizational culture. Also
studied are employee motivation, diversity, group dynamics, and decision-making.
Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Global Business
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The goal of this course is to provide an introduction to international business environment and operations. The course
analyzes the social, economic and political forces shaping multinational business’ activities abroad and uses several
models to understand cultural differences. An analysis of how cultural factors influence and affect decision making and
organizational culture in a global context are the major thrusts of this course.

Prerequisites
EMS
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Entrepreneurship
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The steps leading to the establishment of an independent business involving choice of business, structure, capital,
startup, management practices, legal and financial considerations.
Prerequisites
BU 4110
When Offered:
Every year.

records.title: Business Consulting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
The Business Consulting course covers the complete process of business consulting, from developing business proposal
and mobilizing a consulting team, to producing deliverables and deploying solutions. The course is designed to provide
students with the background and skills needed to pursue a career in consulting.
The course discusses specific applications in such consulting fields as strategy consulting, training, organizational
development, technical, and business development consulting. Specific and practical concepts, tools, techniques and
frameworks are covered that can be used in all forms of consulting and any area of consulting application.
Prerequisites
EMS and Math Proficiency; BU 33502; BU4110; BU3800; BU5196
Recommended: BU4762; BU3010; BU5110

records.title: Advanced Business Analytics
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The main goal of the course is to expose students to cutting-edge analytical techniques and contemporary software
applications used in organizational operations and decision making, including Microsoft Office tools and analytical
software with the focus on their business applications. Students will learn to collect, organize, analyze, and present
information in a comprehensive manner.
Students will understand the concept of databases and their functions, conduct database queries, introduce big data
analytical skills, and perform basic analysis utilizing contemporary analytical packages and programming.
Prerequisites
MA2080 Precalculus; MA2000 Applied Statistics; BU3010 Info Systems for Managers or BU3071; BU3250 Business
Analytics

records.title: Bus Data Vis: Appl & Tech
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course is designed to explore the concept of data visualization, its applications, benefi ts, and importance in various
fi elds. Emphasis is placedon practical applications of data visualization techniques using industry-relevant tools.
Students will engage in hands-on projects with populardata visualization tools and software applications to analyze
business data and communicate insights visually.
Prerequisites
BU/MA 3250
When Offered:
Every SemesterNote:
Required course for new Business Analytics specialization, within B.S. Business Administration degree.

records.title: Business Data Visualization
records.sourceText:
This course is designed to equip business students with the skills and knowledge to effectively use data visualization in
decision-making and communication. Emphasis will be placed on practical applications of data visualization techniques
using industry-relevant tools. Students will engage in hands-on projects to analyze business data and communicate
insights visually.
This course also provides an introduction to the fundamental principles and techniques of data visualization. Students
will explore the concept of data visualization, its applications, benefits, and importance in various fields. The course will
also cover hands-on experience with popular data visualization tools and software applications.
Prerequisites
BU 4160 and BU 3010 or BU 3070 and CS 2521

records.title: Accounting Information Systems
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Examines how management information systems concepts are used to develop accounting information systems that
support decisions by management and other interested groups. Considers the analysis, design utilization, and
evaluation of technology-based and manual-based financial information systems. Focuses on key business processes,
internal controls and risks, flowcharting, and information provided to management.
Prerequisites
BU 3071
, BU 3511

records.title: Intermediate Accounting I
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
An expanded treatment of accounting theory and principles: investigation of accounting for cash and temporary
investments, receivables, inventory costing and evaluation, fixed asset acquisition, depletion and depreciation,
intangible assets, and current liabilities. Emphasis is on the analysis of the recommendations and pronouncements of the
American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and the Financial Accounting Standards Board.

Prerequisites
BU 3511
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Intermediate Accounting II
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
An expanded treatment of accounting theory and principles: investigation of accounting for capital, retained earnings,
pensions, leases, cash flows, and earnings per share. Emphasis is on the analysis of the recommendations and
pronouncements of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and the Financial Accounting Standards
Board.
Prerequisites
BU 4500
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Federal Income Tax l
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
A comprehensive study of tax principles and concepts that apply to income tax planning. The course focuses on the tax
treatment of individuals. Topics include gross income, exclusions, deductions, realization and recognition of income, tax
rates, the treatment of capital assets and the use of tax credits.
Prerequisites
BU 3511

When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Cost Accounting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course provides students with an in-depth understanding of how cost information is gathered, analyzed and
reported for purposes of planning, control and decision-making. Includes a thorough examination of the design and
operation of job order, process and standard cost systems. Related emphasis is also placed on cost behavior, planning
and control of material, labor and overhead costs, activity-based costing, flexible budgeting and variance analysis.
Variable costing, cost-volume-profit-analysis and related techniques are explored as tools to enhance management
decision-making.
Prerequisites
BU 3511
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Global Financial Markets
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course explores the fundamentals of the global financial environment. It covers international capital market, money
market and derivatives markets. Foreign-exchange risk and international portfolio diversification are discussed.
Prerequisites
BU 4762
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Financial Management l
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course provides an introduction to the basic ideas of finance. The primary concepts covered include introductory
accounting knowledge, time value of money, risk-return trade-off, the basic characteristics of financial markets and
financial securities, cost of capital budgeting.
Prerequisites
BU 3502
, MA 2000
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Financial Markets and Institutions
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course focuses on the importance of the financial system in providing liquidity and risk diversification in a globally
interconnected economy. The course develops a series of applications of principles from finance and economics that
explore the connection between financial markets and the economy. Specific topics will include: interest rate
determination, term structure, institutional make-up of capital markets, and risk management of financial institutions.
The recent credit crisis and its origin in subprime mortgages will be reviewed.
Prerequisites
BU 4762
, PE 2430
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Integrated Marketing Communication
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4

This course focuses on the importance of developing synergy of marketing communications practices and relationships
for producers, manufacturers, and retailers with their target consumers. It emphasizes strategic planning and
management of integrated marketing communications covering a variety of functional areas (promotional mix elements)
including advertising, public relations, publicity, direct marketing, digital advertising, marketing and social media, sales
promotion, and event sponsorship, as well as basic principles of brand communications and position strategies.
Prerequisites
BU3800
When Offered:
Occasionally

records.title: International Marketing
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course examines the nature and practice of global marketing management. It includes the problems and issues of
marketing across national boundaries as well as within different national markets. There is an emphasis on the global
environment in which international marketing takes place including product, pricing, supply chain distribution, and
promotion strategies of international marketing managers. It examines ways of integrating and coordinating the firm’s
marketing programs in diverse markets worldwide.
Prerequisites
BU3800Prerequisite/Corequisite
Recommended: PE2430
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Digital Marketing Foundations
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course is designed to integrate the principles of marketing, consumer behavior, and brand strategy in a digital
marketing context. Students will pursue the Google Professional Certificate in Digital Marketing and create integrated
artifacts to demonstrate their learning. Through successful completion of this course, the student will:

1. Conceptualize digital marketing through an industry lens.
2. Understand the foundational principles of Digital Marketing and E-Commerce.
3. Identify opportunities to attract, engage, and interact with customers online.
4. Analyze and design effective digital marketing campaigns.
5. Measure success of digital marketing campaigns.
6. Develop customer loyalty online.
7. Build, launch and manage e-commerce retail stores.
Prerequisites
BU 3800

records.title: Consumer Behavior
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Incorporates concepts from the behavioral sciences that provide a foundation for the study of buyer behavior. The
course evolves through an exploration of the contributions from economics, psychology, sociology and cultural
anthropology that reveal the motivations underlying consumer behavior.
Prerequisites
BU 3800
Must be enrolled in one of the following Fields of Study (Major, Minor, or Concentration):
Accounting
Business Administration
Digital Design Marketing
Finance
Marketing
Women’s and Gender Studies

When Offered:
Every semester.Note:
Must be enrolled in a major, minor or specialization within the School of Business OR with instructor’s approval.

records.title: Operations Management
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Introduction to the theoretical and practical applications of OM. Topics: logistics; facility location layout; acquisition and
replacement forecasting; planning; operation scheduling and control; inventory planning and quality control.
Prerequisites
BU 3010
or BU 3071
, MA 2000
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Business Ethics
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This is a managerially oriented course dealing with the relationship between business and society. A variety of
viewpoints will be presented in the examination of the following topics: social responsibility of business, quality of work
life, ecology and environment, consumerism, business and government, and managerial ethics.
Prerequisites
BU 4110
When Offered:
Occasionally.

records.title: Human Resource Management
records.sourceText:
Course Descriptions - SUNY Old Westbury
Emphasizes the necessity of managing individuals in an organization as resources crucial to survival and success. The
relationship of human resource management to strategic planning and implementation is analyzed. Specific attention is
given to the theories, policies, techniques and methods related to human resource planning, recruitment, selection,
interviewing, training and development, performance, appraisal, separation, labor relations and compensation in
compliance with relevant legislation.
Prerequisites
BU4110 AND BU 3250 or MA 2300 AND MA2000 C- or higher; senior status 88 credits or above.
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Business Intelligence and Data Mining
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course explores the integration of business intelligence (BI) and data mining techniques to extract valuable insights
from large datasets for informed decision-making. Students will learn how to leverage data mining tools and techniques
to analyze and interpret business data, identify patterns, and make data-driven decisions. The course will cover various
aspects of BI, including data warehousing, data preprocessing, data modeling, and the application of data mining
algorithms in a business context. The course covers data preprocessing, modeling, and interpretation of results using
popular programming languages and tools.
Prerequisites
MA 2000
BU3010 OR BU3071
BU3250
CS2521
When Offered:
Spring Only

records.title: Business Strategy and Policy
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Synthesizes the concepts and techniques developed in prior courses. The student is required to apply concepts from
management, accounting, marketing, economics, and finance using the casework and/or simulation approach.
Prerequisites
BU 3800
, BU 4110
, BU 4762
Senior Status - 88 credits or higher

When Offered:
Every semester. Must be taken in student’s senior year.

records.title: Management Seminar
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Selected current issues in the field are discussed. Emphasis will be on student research and critical analysis of topics.
Topics may vary from year to year.
Prerequisites
MA 2000
, BU 4110
When Offered:
Occasionally.

records.title: Leadership
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course is designed to provide an overview of the fundamental concepts of basic leadership models and theories, as
well as an in-depth understanding of contemporary issues and perspectives on Leadership and Supervision. Emphasis
will be on attempting to understand and develop the skills, attitudes, and knowledge bases required to effectively lead
and influence others in the global environment of the 21st century.
Prerequisites
BU4110
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Internship in Business Administration
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4

Designed for students who want experience in the work place participating in the management environment. This is an
excellent opportunity to prepare for a career in the field. Open to Business Administration majors only.
Prerequisites
Senior status; approval by Director of Career Services
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Essentials of Government and Nonprofit Accounting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
This course is an introduction to government and nonprofit accounting. Fund accounting theory as well as financial
statement presentation will be discussed for both government and nonprofit entities. The course also presents an
overview of government auditing standards.
Prerequisites
BU 4500
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Forensics & Fraud Examination
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Course Description - A study of the role of the forensic accountant in different facets of fraud examination and
deterrence, such as the design and implementation of controls, fraud schemes and devices, cybercrime, criminology,
corruption, bribery, financial statement fraud, interviewing and interrogation, as well as the roles of various key players
in a fraud examination, such as the litigation support team, valuation analysts, and investigators. This course will
introduce students to the various skillsets needed for success in the forensic accounting profession, including data
analysis, interviewing, critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving.
Prerequisites

BU 4510
When Offered:
Fall / Spring Semesters

records.title: Financial Accounting Research
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
This course will provide a critical update and evaluation of recent development in financial reporting and accounting
theory. The emphasis will be on an in depth evaluation and application of some of the more advanced topics that may
have been briefly covered in Intermediate Accounting 2, such as derivatives, cash flow, pensions, leases, accounting
errors and changes, and disclosure. Extensive use will be made of the FASB Codification of accounting standards and
case studies
Prerequisites
BU 4510
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Fundamentals of International Accounting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
A discussion of the evolution of international accounting principles and practices. International Financial Reporting
Standards (IFRS) and reference to accounting and reporting requirements in selected countries will be covered. Current
developments and implications for multinational organizations are also addressed.
Prerequisites
BU 4510

When Offered:
Occasionally

records.title: Advanced Accounting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course covers accounting for partnerships: formation, operation, dissolution, and liquidation. There is an in-depth
analysis of business combinations including statutory mergers, consolidations, and acquisition of subsidiaries,
preparation of consolidated financial statements including the equity method and elimination entries. Additionally, the
course includes an introduction to foreign currency translation and transactions, the SEC, and Sarbanes-Oxley.
Prerequisites
BU 4510
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Auditing
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Study of the professional ethics and possible legal liability of the auditor. Examination of current auditing theory and
techniques and their application to specific balance sheet and income statement accounts to obtain evidence that
management’s financial statements are fairly presented, including the generally accepted auditing standards, role of
internal control, uses of sampling, effects of information technology, and the various reports rendered by auditors.
Prerequisites
BU 4510
When Offered:
Every semester. Must be taken in student’s last semester.

records.title: Foundations of Accounting Information Systems
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
Examines the fundamental roles and functions of accounting information systems in providing support for decisions by
management and other interested groups. Topics include database concepts, accounting data flow, and business
processes. Students will learn how to apply software such as Microsoft Access in designing their own systems.
Prerequisites
BU 3010
or BU 3071
, BU 4500
When Offered:
Every year.

records.title: Financial Statement Analysis
records.sourceText:
Credits: 2
An advanced level course covering the analytical tools necessary for conducting a financial analysis of a business and its
financial statements. The course will focus on selecting the appropriate analytical tools and the effective use of notes to
the financial statements for making financial decisions about a business. Topics include ratio and trend analysis, as well
as an examination of annual reports, 10K and 10Q filings.
Prerequisites
BU 4510
When Offered:
Occasionally.

records.title: Internship in Accounting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Designed for students who want experience in the work place participating in the accounting environment. This is an
excellent opportunity to prepare for a career in the field. Open to Accounting majors only.

Prerequisites
Senior standing; approval by Director of Career Services
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Financial Modeling and Forecasting
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The course is aimed at giving students a working knowledge of the analytical tools that are important in the decisions
firms regularly make Emphasis will be placed on the performance goals of the firm, the forecasting of investment
returns and firm cash flows, and the estimation of investment firm risk parameters. Regression analysis, along with
other statistical modeling tools where necessary, will be used to estimate relationships among economic variables, and as
a forecasting tool. The course is aimed at consolidating knowledge gained in other functional areas of business. While
knowledge of quantitative techniques is presupposed, the emphasis is more on economic intuition as a practical
problem-solving tool.
Prerequisites
BU 4762, PE 2420
, PE 2430
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Investment Management and Security Analysis
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Study of theories, techniques and approaches for determining the values of major types of securities including
derivation of capitalization rates, forecasting of earnings and technical analysis. Evaluation of the dividend, capital
leverage controversies and the efficient market hypothesis. Introduction to modern portfolio theories and investment
strategies.

Prerequisites
BU 4762
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Corporate Finance
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course introduces students to the principle of maximization of the firm’s value in a world with uncertainty. It
covers firm’s capital structure and dividend policy, cash flow management, short-term financing, merger and acquisition
and leasing.
Prerequisites
BU 4762
When Offered:
Every year.

records.title: Futures and Options Markets
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This class will provide students with a basic knowledge of derivatives in options, futures, and forwards markets. Topics
include option valuation models, principles of forward and futures pricing, structure of markets for derivative
securities, and strategies for hedging and speculation.
Prerequisites
BU 4762
When Offered:
Every year.

records.title: Seminar in Finance
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Discussion of topics in finance chosen by instructor.
Prerequisites

records.title: Financial Management l
records.sourceText:
BU4792 AND PE2420 AND PE2430
When Offered:
Occasionally.

records.title: CFA Level I Exam Preparation
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course examines ethical and professional standards and reviews financial analysis tools including economics;
quantitative analysis; financial accounting and statement analysis; markets and institutions; and asset valuation and
portfolio management techniques.
Prerequisites
BU 4762
, BU 5760
, BU 5771
When Offered:
Occasionally.

records.title: Internship in Finance
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
Designed for students who want experience in the work place participating in the finance environment. This is an
excellent opportunity to prepare for a career in the field. Open to Business Administration, Finance specialization majors
only.

Prerequisites
Senior status; approval by Director of Career Services
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Marketing Research
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
The course examines qualitative and quantitative marketing research techniques. It provides a step by step coverage of a
research project including problem definition, research design, sampling, questionnaire construction, data analysis, and
report preparation. Students will design and execute a small scale research project.
Prerequisites
MA 2000
, BU 3800
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Strategic Marketing
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course applies the marketing strategy concept as a management tool for optimizing performance. It focuses on the
marketer’s deployment of resources to achieve goals in a competitive environment. Students will be applying
knowledge gained in other courses to analyze case studies. In addition, the course explores current marketing topics
such as social media and business analytics and integrates them into strategic planning.
Prerequisites
BU 3800

When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Brand Theory and Strategy
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4
This course focuses on how brands are created and managed within the marketing process. Using an interdisciplinary
marketing and social science perspective, students analyze the cultural system of brand identity generated by product
manipulation and consumer choice, creating value for both buyer and corporation. Marketing policies are evaluated
through an analysis of product development, distribution and pricing with particular focus on the newest
communication tools in advertising, public relations and sales promotions.
Prerequisites
BU 4851
NOTE: Must be enrolled in one of the following Fields of Study (Major, Minor, or Concentration):
Accounting
Business Administration
Digital Design Marketing
Finance
Marketing
Women’s and Gender Studies
When Offered:
Every semester.

records.title: Marketing Seminar
records.sourceText:
Credits: 4

A program tailored to the needs and interests of students of marketing, advertising, and public policy issues. Students
complete an actual business project related to marketing.
Prerequisites
BU 3800
, Senior Standing.

Occasionally.

When Offered:
Every semester.
